newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-KONSTANTINOV UPGRADED FROM CRITICAL TO SERIOUS.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-KONSTANTINOV UPGRADED FROM CRITICAL TO SERIOUS.

text.p: Detroit Red Wings defenceman Vladimir Konstantinov is gradually emerging from a coma and his condition was upgraded from critical to serious, doctors treating the Russian star said Sunday.
At a news briefing, doctors at William Beaumont Hospital reported that Konstantinov no longer needed a ventilator to breathe.
Dr James Robbins said the ventilator, which Konstantinov had relied upon since the June 13 limousine crash, had been removed from his room.
"He is breathing 100 percent on his own," Robbins said.
The team's Russian trainer Sergei Mnatsakanov was also upgraded to serious and showing signs of coming out of coma, doctors said.

Konstantinov, Mnatsakanov and Red Wings defenceman Slava Fetisov were injured when the limousine they were riding in crashed into a tree just six days after Detroit won the Stanley Cup, ending a 42-year title drought.
Fetisov sustained a bruised lung and lacerations to his chest. Konstantinov and Mnatsakanov suffered serious head injuries and have been in a coma since the accident.
But doctors said the tough as nails Russian defenceman is now consistently opening his eyes, is able to follow simple commands, and his vital signs are stable.
Mnatsakanov is in the process of being weaned from a ventilator. He is also showing steady improvements in responding to commands from family and doctors, and his vital signs are stable.
"No further surgery is needed for neurological injuries for either patient," said neurosurgeon Karol Zalkalik.

A rehabilitation team consisting of doctors, physical and speech therapists are working with the 30-year-old Konstantinov and Mnatsakanov to provide stimulation and educate the families of the patients.
"Both the Konstantinovs and Mnatsakanovs have great emotional and spiritual strength, and if it is possible to will a person back to health, it will be done in this case," said Robbins.
Konstantinov, who was the blue line anchor of Detroit's sensational defensive play in the run to the Stanley Cup, has also undergone surgeries to his right elbow to repair a tendon and remove debris.
The limousine driver, 28-year-old Richard Gnida, who was driving without a license after having his revoked, was released from the hospital two days after the accident.
It is believed he fell asleep at the wheel but police have yet to file charges or make any arrests.
Konstantinov, nicknamed "The Vladinator" for his punishing physical style, was a finalist for the Norris Trophy as the National Hockey League's top defencemen this year.
